10. Decisionmaking by the three levels of Government (Federal, State, and Local) concerning ORVs
Decisionmaking concerning ORVs represents a coordinated effort by the Department of the Interior, with participation and assistance from State and local governments.
In accordance with the Department's policy of public participation in the rulemaking process, all levels of government were involved in the development of the environmental statement and regulations concerning ORV use on Interior lands.
In addition to the advance public notices, meetings, and hearings, the Department held scheduled meetings with State and County government officials to obtain their direct input in the development of the ORV regulations.
The Department also recognizes the importance of its officials and land managers having adequate authority to take appropriate actions on the scene in order to protect the resources of the lands under their administration and has made provisions in its guidelines and regulations authorizing such actions.
11. Clarification of intensive use of public lands
As used in this statement, intensive use represents use in which large numbers of vehicles use a limited quantity of designated trails and areas on a high frequency scale during certain time periods and/or seasons of the year. For example, weekend snowmobile use may occur on an intensive scale during the winter season on designated routes in some of the National Parks located in the Snowbelt States. The locations and conditions under which these uses are permitted are set forth in Departmental regulations.
On the other hand, extensive use represents use in which the lands available are not so limited in quantity and, therefore, large numbers of vehicles can be accommodated without requiring intensive use of any particular portions of these lands. The vast holdings of public lands under the jurisdiction of the Department's Bureau of Land Management provide examples in which extensive ORV use may occur on a broad base since the majority of these lands are open to the public for multiple uses, including ORV use. Motorcycle enthusiasts and those engaged in the hobby of rockhounding in the Western States represent two groups engaging in extensive use of Interior lands on a broad scale. These recreationists use various kinds of ORV's, including jeeps, dunebuggies, campers, ATV's, pickup trucks, and the like. Primarily, these activities reach their peak during the spring, summer, and fall seasons and the areas covered consist of thousands of acres of public lands.
In summary, the types of resources on specific public lands and the adverse environmental impacts resulting from specific types of ORV use on these lands will determine whether certain lands are open for intensive or extensive ORV use. Lands may be classified as open, restricted, or closed to ORV use, depending on whether such use would be damaging to the resources of those lands. Therefore, the land classification given to specific lands will limit the degree of ORV use. Whether lands are used intensively or extensively and the specific types of ORV use permitted are sometimes contingent upon the seasons of the year.
